title: Consolidate checkpoint registry and decouple tokenizer initialization timeline
text:
Consolidate checkpoint registry and decouple tokenizer initialization timeline

description:
Problem: Our model ingestion pipeline has grown ad-hoc: multiple checkpoint descriptors, scattered shard activation logic, and tokenizer initialization tightly coupled to weight deserialization. This causes unpredictable cold-start latency, duplicated format adapters, and complex fallback code paths during rollouts.

Goal: Replace ad-hoc detectors with a single Checkpoint Registry (manifest v2) that offers a metadata-first view of a model package, and refactor the boot sequence so tokenizer construction is decoupled from full weight hydration. The aim is to reduce median load time for common package shapes by 20-40%, eliminate duplicate format checks, and make shard hot-swap safer for canary rollouts.

acceptance_criteria:
Add Checkpoint Registry service that exposes a stable manifest v2 for every supported package format
Model boot sequence updated: metadata scan -> tokenizer lazy-init -> critical-shard activation -> background hydrate remaining shards
Tokenizer no longer blocks initial request handling; we can serve non-tokenizer paths (embeddings/rerank) on metadata alone
Legacy format adapters adapt into registry via a single adapter wrapper; no direct format checks outside registry
End-to-end tests covering atomic shard swap, failure rollback, and tokenizer fallback present in CI
Benchmarks show >=20% median cold-start improvement on common 2-4 shard packages in CI cluster

implementation_plan:
1) Design manifest v2 spec (fields: package_id, formats, shard_map, compatibility_flags, tokenizer_signature, quick-checksum)
2) Implement a Checkpoint Registry module that normalizes existing format adapters behind a single interface
3) Change model loader boot sequence: metadata scan -> register in registry -> start tokenizer factory in background but allow minimal operations with tokenizer-placeholder -> activate critical shards (embedding/serving paths) -> hydrate remaining shards asynchronously
4) Add adapter shim that translates legacy checkpoint readers to registry shape (single place to add new formats)
5) Implement atomic shard swap primitives used by hot-reload and canary rollouts
6) Add telemetry: per-phase timing (scan/tokenizer-init/shard-activation/hydrate), registry cache hit rate, adapter fallback counts
7) Add unit and e2e tests; run benchmarks on staging and tune concurrency/IO knobs
8) Rollout: opt-in feature flag for runtime-1.21, progressive ramp to 25%->50%->100% with metrics guardrails

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Tokenizer deferred init could cause mid-request latency when first used. Mitigation: start tokenizer factory eagerly after metadata scan and pre-warm when request patterns indicate imminent tokenizer usage.
Risk: Registry normalization may miss edge-case formats. Mitigation: maintain adapter shim and a validation step that rejects unknown manifest fields; add telemetry for adapter fallbacks.
Risk: Background hydration might contend with serving IO. Mitigation: rate-limit background reads and use priority queues so serving-critical shards always have priority.
Risk: Canary rollback complexity for atomic swap. Mitigation: implement explicit swap transaction with fast rollback path and small-step canaries initially (single-tenant first).

testing_and_validation:
Unit tests for Checkpoint Registry adapter surface and manifest correctness
Integration tests that boot sample packages (legacy and new) exercising deferred tokenizer path
Load tests that simulate cold-starts across package sizes (1, 4, 16 shards) and measure per-phase timings
Chaos test: abort halfway through hydration and verify rollback invariants
Manual verification on staging: smoke runs of gen/chat/embeddings routes behind feature flag

rollout_plan:
Stage 0: merge behind feature flag; only dev/staging clusters enabled
Stage 1: enable for non-production tenant subset (10%) for 48h, monitor metrics: load_time, error_rate, tokenizer_miss_latency
Stage 2: expand to 50% with automated rollback if any metric deviates beyond thresholds
Stage 3: full enable and remove legacy adapter paths after 2 weeks of stable telemetry

metrics_to_track:
checkpoint_registry_hit_rate
boot_phase_scan_ms
tokenizer_init_ms
critical_shard_activation_ms
background_hydration_io_mb
canary_swap_failure_count

comments:
2026-02-24 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket; initial spec drafted. Captured goals and success metrics.
2026-02-26 - Marco Ruiz: Spike results posted - metadata-first scan cuts first-phase work by ~18% on sample set. Link to prototype results in links.
2026-03-02 - Design review with Lina (Product): Agreed to preserve exact manifest fields needed for console rollouts; Lina requested an explicit field for 'compatibility_tier'.
2026-03-05 - Security: quick review - no secrets in manifest; recommend a review for KMS integration later. Marked security_review_required=false for initial rollout.
2026-03-08 - Code review (PR #7894): Registry API landed; requested changes around adapter error semantics; Marco responding.
2026-03-10 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented tokenizer factory background start; added feature flag. Queueing integration tests.

qa_notes:
When testing, validate both legacy and new-format packages. Use the sample packages in /testdata/checkpoints.
Force background-hydration throttling to validate serving precedence for critical shards.
Simulate tokenizer-only workloads (rerank/embeddings) to confirm they can proceed on metadata alone.
